content: The medication is indicated for the treatment of the following conditions: 1. Rheumatoid Arthritis: Adalimumab is prescribed for moderate-to-severe active rheumatoid arthritis at a dose of 40 mg subcutaneously every two weeks. 2. Psoriatic Arthritis: It is used to treat active psoriatic arthritis with the same dosing regimen of 40 mg subcutaneously every two weeks. 3. Ankylosing Spondylitis: The medication is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms of active ankylosing spondylitis, also at 40 mg subcutaneously every two weeks. 4. Chronic Plaque Psoriasis: For moderate-to-severe chronic plaque psoriasis in patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy, and when systemic therapies are inappropriate, the initial dose is 80 mg subcutaneously once, followed by 40 mg subcutaneously every two weeks starting one week later. Use beyond one year has not been evaluated in controlled clinical studies. It is also indicated for patients with moderate-to-severe fingernail psoriasis. 5. Crohn’s Disease (Adults): Adalimumab is used to reduce signs and symptoms and to induce and maintain clinical remission in moderately-to-severely active Crohn’s disease in patients with inadequate response to conventional therapy or those intolerant to infliximab. The induction dose is 160 mg subcutaneously (administered as four 40 mg injections on day 1 or two 40 mg injections daily over two consecutive days), followed by 80 mg subcutaneously two weeks later (day 15). Maintenance therapy begins at week 4 (day 29) with 40 mg subcutaneously every two weeks. Continued use is recommended only if clinical remission is evident by eight weeks of therapy. Effectiveness beyond one year has not been established in controlled studies. 6. Crohn’s Disease (Pediatrics): For pediatric patients with moderately-to-severely active Crohn’s disease who have had an inadequate response to corticosteroids or immunomodulators, the safety and efficacy are not established for children under six years of age. 7. Ulcerative Colitis: Adalimumab is indicated for moderately-to-severely active ulcerative colitis in patients aged five years and older. Safety and efficacy are not established for children under five years of age. 8. Hidradenitis Suppurativa: It is indicated for moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa (Hurley stage 2 and 3 disease) in adults and adolescents aged 12 years or older who weigh at least 30 kg. Safety and efficacy are not established for children under 12 years of age. 9. Noninfectious Uveitis: The medication is used to treat noninfectious intermediate, posterior, and panuveitis in adults and children aged two years or older. Safety and efficacy are not established for children under two years of age or those weighing less than 10 kg. 10. Polyarticular Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: Adalimumab is indicated for moderately-to-severely active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis and may be administered with methotrexate, glucocorticoids, NSAIDs, or analgesics. Safety and efficacy are not established for children under two years of age or those weighing less than 10 kg. Drug Interactions and Contraindications: Immunosuppressive Effects: Adalimumab increases the risk of infections when combined with other immunosuppressive agents such as abatacept, anakinra, alefacept, and infliximab. These combinations are contraindicated or should be avoided. Vaccines: Adalimumab reduces the effectiveness of live vaccines (e.g., BCG, yellow fever, varicella, measles-mumps-rubella) and inactivated vaccines (e.g., influenza, pneumococcal, hepatitis A/B). Live vaccines are contraindicated during therapy due to the risk of infection. Other Biologics: Combining adalimumab with other biologics (e.g., vedolizumab, ustekinumab, tocilizumab) or JAK inhibitors (e.g., baricitinib) increases immunosuppressive effects and infection risk. These combinations should be avoided or monitored closely. Methotrexate: Methotrexate reduces the clearance of adalimumab, but no dosage adjustment is necessary. Neonatal Fc Receptor Binding: Close monitoring is recommended. Special Considerations: Long-Term Use: The safety and efficacy of adalimumab for certain conditions, such as chronic plaque psoriasis and Crohn’s disease, have not been evaluated beyond one year in controlled studies. Immune Competence: Patients receiving immunosuppressive therapy should avoid vaccination during treatment. If vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during therapy, revaccination is recommended three months after discontinuation if immune competence is restored. Caution with Herbal Supplements: Interactions with herbal supplements like astragalus, echinacea, and maitake may alter immunosuppressive effects. Use caution and monitor closely. This information highlights the importance of careful patient selection, monitoring, and adherence to contraindications to optimize the therapeutic benefits of adalimumab while minimizing risks.
